feed.title: BrewSLM engineering blog
feed.subtitle: Engineering notes on small language model fine-tuning infrastructure.

entry.title: Narrative in, JSON out: a 1.5B accident-report extractor that knows when to say null
entry.summary: A 1.5B model fine-tuned to turn NTSB aviation accident narratives into a 13-field JSON record. 0.959 field accuracy on 1,234 pre-registered test narratives against 0.494 for the base model, and null when the text doesn't say. All three seeds passed. Every number, including where it still fails.

entry.title: Teaching a 1.5B model to read IRS Pub 17: two misses, one pass
entry.summary: Part 2 of the Pub 17 run. A 1.5B model fine-tuned to answer from retrieved passages beat the same base model reading the same passages: 0.688 vs 0.570 on 157 pre-registered questions, all three seeds better. Every number, including the two attempts that missed.

entry.title: The check said don't fine-tune. We did anyway. It was right.
entry.summary: Same 41 questions, same judge: base model 0.17, base + retrieved passages 0.73, fine-tuned on 405 pairs 0.02. A pre-training check called it before training.

entry.title: Build a sensitive-data detector from zero, with no labelled data
entry.summary: Step by step: a model that finds PCI, GDPR, HIPAA and custom sensitive data with exact offsets, from an empty project and no labels. Every number real.

entry.title: Inside the task-aware eval handler dispatcher
entry.summary: One generic 'pass rate' metric flatters classification and lies about NER. Here's how BrewSLM dispatches to the metric shape that matches the task.

entry.title: Why the schema introspector beats hand-written converters
entry.summary: We shipped a 175-line BIO-to-spans converter for the Kaggle PII dataset. Then we threw it away and built a column sniffer. Here's why the sniffer wins.

entry.title: Gamifying a dev tool without making it a toy
entry.summary: Most gamified dev tools feel infantilizing. We tried it anyway. Here are the design rules we landed on and what we explicitly refused to do.
